title: Step Supporting Observation Unit Lifecycle Contract

scope.purpose: Define lifecycle responsibilities and boundaries for Observation Unit instances, including readiness, activation eligibility, ongoing observation, quiescence, reuse, release, and preservation of independently retained observation records.
scope.appliesTo: Each concrete Step specialization that provisions, acquires, admits, reuses, or releases Observation Unit instances.

separation: Observation Unit instance lifetime is distinct from each association lifetime.
Observation Unit instance lifetime is distinct from each observation activity or subscription activation lifetime.
Observation Unit instance lifetime is distinct from the retention lifetime of emitted observation records.
Ending an association does not automatically release an instance.
Retaining observation records does not require retaining the Observation Unit runtime instance.
lifecyclePrinciples.authority: The owning Step Composition owns lifecycle decisions and coordinates lifecycle transitions. The concrete Observation Unit implementation performs its own initialization, activation mechanics, shutdown, and resource-release mechanics.
lifecyclePrinciples.specialization: The common contract defines lifecycle obligations and conceptual milestones only. It does not impose one universal state machine, pool, scheduler, subscription mechanism, or resource-management implementation.

lifecycleMilestones.name: ProvisionedOrAcquired
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: An Observation Unit instance has been created or obtained and has a stable observationUnitIdentity.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Prepared
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: Specialization-required configuration, dependencies, capture resources, or observation interfaces have been prepared.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Ready
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: The instance satisfies its declared technical readiness conditions for admission or activation.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Admitted
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: Step Composition has authorized the instance for use within the owning Step.

lifecycleMilestones.name: AvailableOrInUse
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: The instance is available for observation activity or is currently performing/servicing one or more activities.

lifecycleMilestones.name: ObservingOrSubscribed
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: Where applicable, the instance has an active sampling loop, event subscription, callback registration, or other ongoing observation mechanism.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Quiescing
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: Step Composition has stopped authorizing new activities and is coordinating termination or reconciliation of active observation work and pending emissions.

lifecycleMilestones.name: RetainedForReuse
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: The instance remains available for possible reuse under the concrete Step's reset, isolation, and readiness requirements.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Released
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: The instance's release operation has completed successfully and the instance is no longer available for invocation or observation.

rules: The milestones are descriptive lifecycle concepts, not a mandatory enum or linear state machine.
A concrete specialization may omit, combine, repeat, or refine milestones where its lifecycle mechanics require it.
The order and transition conditions are defined by the concrete Step specialization.
A subscription or ongoing observer may remain active across multiple observed events without treating each event as a new instance lifecycle transition.
Released means successful completion of release; a failed or indeterminate release remains an unresolved lifecycle outcome and must not be labelled Released.

stepComposition: Decides whether an Observation Unit instance is provisioned, acquired, admitted, activated, available, reused, quiesced, or released.
Determines whether the instance is eligible for new observation activities and which associations may be used.
Coordinates association termination/deactivation with observation activity shutdown.
Defines instance reuse, reset, isolation, concurrency, and release policy for the concrete Step.
Ensures active work and emitted-record custody are reconciled before successful release.
observationUnitImplementation: Performs specialization-specific preparation and readiness checks.
Implements technical activation/deactivation, sampling, subscription, callback, and shutdown mechanics where applicable.
Reports readiness, activation, quiescence, and release outcomes through its declared interaction boundary.
Ensures resources it owns are released according to the specialization.
associationTarget: May expose or withdraw its own observation surface or event source under its own contract.
Does not acquire Observation Unit lifecycle authority merely by being an association target.

rules: An instance may be associated or admitted only under the concrete Step's lifecycle and association preconditions.
Admission is a Step Composition decision and is distinct from technical readiness.
Association establishment does not necessarily activate observation immediately.
An instance may be admitted and available while having no active association or observation activity if the concrete Step permits it.
The concrete Step defines whether a persistent subscription/callback is activated per association, per activity, or for a broader instance lifetime.
The instance must not accept new work after Step Composition has withdrawn authorization for new observation activity.
Each observation activity or subscription activation has a lifetime distinct from the Observation Unit instance.
The concrete Step defines whether activities are short-lived calls, long-lived subscriptions, periodic sampling processes, or another model.
The concrete Step defines handling of concurrent activities, callback reentrancy, queued events, buffering, backpressure, and cancellation where applicable.
An instance may remain alive after an activity completes and may be reused according to its specialization.
An active association does not require continuous observation unless the concrete Step explicitly activates a continuous mechanism.
The instance must expose enough readiness/availability information for Step Composition to determine whether it can safely accept new activities or enter quiescence.

preReleaseConditions: Step Composition has stopped authorizing new observation activities for the instance.
All associations that could authorize new activities have been ended, deactivated, or otherwise rendered unusable according to the Association Contract.
Active calls, callbacks, sampling cycles, subscriptions, and asynchronous observation work have completed, been cancelled, or been explicitly reconciled under the specialization.
Queued or in-flight source events and produced-but-not-yet-accepted observation records have been delivered, transferred to a named recovery owner, or explicitly resolved under the custody contract.
Target-side registrations, callbacks, subscriptions, handles, and resources owned by the Observation Unit have been detached or scheduled for safe release.
The specialization's reuse/reset and resource-isolation requirements have been satisfied if reuse rather than release is selected.
releaseRules: Step Composition decides when release is appropriate and coordinates the release operation.
The Observation Unit implementation performs the mechanics of releasing resources it owns.
Successful release is recorded only after the implementation confirms completion under the concrete release contract.
A failed or indeterminate release remains unresolved; it must not be treated as successful or silently retried if retry could duplicate or corrupt release effects.
Release does not erase observation records already accepted by their destination or retained under the Step's observation retention policy.
Release does not require retaining the runtime instance merely because historical records reference observationUnitIdentity.

rules: An instance may be reused only if the concrete Step specialization permits it and the instance satisfies readiness and isolation requirements for the next use.
The concrete Step defines whether reuse requires reconfiguration, reset, re-subscription, or fresh association identities.
A reused instance retains observationUnitIdentity only when it is the same runtime instance under the identity contract.
New associations and observation activities receive new identities; prior association and activity provenance is not reused.
Reuse must not cause observations from a prior association, target, or invocation to be attributed to a later one.
The common contract does not mandate an object pool, reference counting, locks, or a global lifecycle manager.
Preparation, readiness, activation, quiescence, or release failure is a lifecycle outcome, not an observation payload or validation outcome.
No universal lifecycle error taxonomy, retry, replacement, compensation, or fallback policy is prescribed.
Step Composition determines the concrete recovery response, including whether to retry, replace, isolate, retain unresolved state, or terminate the Step path.
If release outcome is indeterminate, instance identity and release status remain unresolved until reconciled; it must not be treated as Released or reused without an explicit safety determination.
Lifecycle failure does not invalidate observation records already accepted by their destination.
Records produced before a lifecycle failure remain subject to their established custody and retention contracts.
Observation records and provenance may outlive the association and the runtime instance.

Retention of observation data must not implicitly retain runtime handles, callback registrations, subscription objects, borrowed references, or leases that prevent release, unless an independently specified requirement exists.
If a record refers to instance-owned memory or resources, the specialization must define how that content is detached or materialized before those resources are released.
Historical observationUnitIdentity and observationUnitAssociationIdentity remain interpretable after release and dissociation.
The retention owner and retention policy are defined by the concrete Step or destination, not by the mere fact that the Observation Unit produced the record.

required: Define provisioning/acquisition and instance identity generation.
Define preparation and technical readiness criteria.
Define admission and activation authority and conditions.
Define the lifetime of calls, subscriptions, callbacks, sampling loops, and other observation activities.
Define association activation/deactivation behavior and coordination with association termination.
Define concurrency, reentrancy, cancellation, buffering, and backpressure requirements where applicable.
Define quiescence conditions, including in-flight work, queued events, and pending record custody.
Define successful release confirmation and indeterminate/failure reconciliation.
Define reuse/reset/isolation requirements if reuse is permitted.
Define ownership and release of subscriptions, callbacks, target handles, and other runtime resources.
Define observation-record detachment, custody, retention owner, and historical provenance preservation.
specializationRequirements.completionRule: A concrete lifecycle specialization is complete when instance identity, readiness/admission, activity and association interaction, quiescence, custody reconciliation, reuse, release, and historical evidence independence are explicit.

explicitNonGoals: No universal linear lifecycle state machine or mandatory lifecycle enum.
No mandatory object pool, factory, service locator, scheduler, reference counter, or global lifecycle manager.
No assumption that every Observation Unit is a continuously running observer or subscription.
No assumption that every Observation Unit is stateless or stateful.
No automatic release when the last association ends.
No retention of runtime instances solely to preserve historical observation records.
No universal retry, replacement, fallback, or compensation policy.

references.relationship: Observation activity, output, record custody, and provenance obligations.

Observation records remain outside the common Step result and have an independent retention boundary.

frameworkCoordination.conformance: This contract specializes the shared Step Composition coordination invariants. Where the shared contract defines only conceptual identity roles or lifecycle distinctions, this document supplies the component-specific identity names, semantics, mechanics, and constraints.
frameworkCoordination.precedence: The common contract governs cross-cutting Step Composition coordination invariants. This specialized contract governs component-specific behavior and mechanics. Neither contract changes the component pattern?s distinct behavioral result semantics.
